answer: Whether agents manage a trellis, irrigate an oasis, or monitor a reef, their marketplace can weight governance votes by escrowed stake rather than account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting power. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens for the voting period, tying up capital and sacrificing its use elsewhere; creating identities alone adds no power.
